spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **Risk-Based Authentication (RBA)** evaluates contextual signals at login time in **<50 ms**—device posture/cookie, IP reputation (Tor/VPN/residential proxy ASN), impossible travel (>800 km/h), and JA4 TLS fingerprint—and routes.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Real-Time Risk Scoring & Authentication Decision Tree (LOW RISK (0-29) -> MEDIUM (30-69) -> HIGH (70-100)); Why WebAuthn Defeats Evilginx Reverse-Proxy Phishing (User Browser -> evil-login.com -> corp-idp.com).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare MFA factors across phishing resistance, UX, and recovery complexity. Even with WebAuthn, a stolen session cookie (`Set-Cookie`) can be replayed from another machine.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Connect adaptive MFA to OAuth2/OIDC flows, JWT validation, and zero-trust service authentication.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement MFA & Risk-Based Authentication without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When untrusted callers cross a trust boundary, static SMS/push MFA fails against AiTM reverse-proxy phishing and push bombing; pair a <50 ms risk-scoring engine with origin-bound FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys and number-matched push fallback.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.
